title: Visual exploration patterns of human figures in action: an eye tracker study with art paintings
abstracted_dimensions: social action in an image is more legible when one participant's action corresponds to another participant's reaction
faces attract viewing in socially interactive scenes while acting body parts help specify individual action
gaze can establish dyadic mutual attention or triadic attention involving a shared target
body orientation and distance participate in interaction perception but do not independently prove relationship or personality
action timing and perceptual consequence contribute to a viewer's sense that one participant responded to another
limitations: the anchor experiment used ten historical paintings and forty-four nonexpert adult viewers, so it does not establish a universal composition formula
the supporting gaze experiment used controlled virtual interaction rather than static subculture illustration
the supporting proxemics study measured live dyads and subjective interaction quality rather than artwork preference
relationship, status, affection, and personality must not be inferred from pose, gaze, orientation, overlap, or distance alone
reuse_note: Only abstract attention, complementary-action, shared-target, and contingency mechanisms were retained; no source image, composition, person, character, protected design, or prose was copied.

mechanisms.statement: stage every claimed relationship through a directed action with a visible target and a reaction or consequence
distinguish mutual dyadic attention from triadic attention organized around a shared object or event
route the first read through faces for social orientation and the second read through acting hands bodies and targets for event comprehension
treat distance overlap and body orientation as compositional variables rather than evidence of personality affection rank or consent
give each ensemble member an active contribution counteraction decision or observable response instead of a decorative pose
use a suspended response or aftermath trace to make temporal contingency legible inside a still image
claim care conflict authority or trust only when action target and consequence jointly support that reading
separate character hierarchy from human worth by using focal priority to explain the event rather than to diminish secondary figures

illustration_evidence_definitions.ensemble_directed_action_vector: A limb, tool, carried object, or motion trace visibly begins at one actor and points toward a specific target.
illustration_evidence_definitions.ensemble_target_contact_or_avoidance: The target visibly receives, blocks, redirects, approaches, or avoids the directed action rather than merely occupying nearby space.
illustration_evidence_definitions.ensemble_reaction_consequence: A changed grip, displaced object, altered stance, opened path, or other visible result confirms that the action affected its target.
illustration_evidence_definitions.ensemble_gaze_triangle: Two participants and one shared object or event form a readable triangle of attention, with the target itself visible.
illustration_evidence_definitions.ensemble_role_silhouette_separation: Each active participant retains a distinct readable outer contour at thumbnail scale even where bodies or props overlap.
illustration_evidence_definitions.ensemble_reciprocal_orientation: Head, torso, hands, or tools orient in complementary directions that support the shown exchange without being treated as personality proof.
illustration_evidence_definitions.ensemble_shared_task_prop: One neutral prop or work surface is visibly manipulated by more than one participant and anchors their complementary roles.
illustration_evidence_definitions.ensemble_afteraction_trace: A falling fragment, transferred item, moved chair, opened barrier, or disturbed surface records the immediate consequence of the interaction.

candidate_definitions.asymmetric_help_with_response: One figure offers concrete aid and the target visibly accepts, redirects, or declines it, preserving agency on both sides.
candidate_definitions.negotiated_object_exchange: An object moves or is contested between participants through readable hand paths, grips, and a resulting ownership or placement state.
candidate_definitions.cooperative_shared_attention: Participants coordinate around the same visible target through gaze and task contact rather than smiling or proximity alone.
candidate_definitions.competitive_counteraction: One directed action meets a visible block, redirection, or counter-move with neither side reduced to a decorative victim pose.
candidate_definitions.interrupted_group_action: A shared action is visibly disrupted, and every principal figure shows a distinct response to the same interruption.
candidate_definitions.ensemble_event_focal_hierarchy: Contrast, scale, and overlap prioritize the event's causal chain while preserving readable secondary actions and silhouettes.

compatibility: combine gaze with a visible shared target when claiming joint or shared attention
combine proximity with reciprocal action and consequence before suggesting affiliation or conflict
pair focal hierarchy with silhouette separation so secondary participants remain legible
pair a helping or protective action with an observable response from the target
use a shared prop to connect participants only when each hand path and task role can be followed
conflicts: do not treat closeness touching or overlap as proof of romance consent trust or kinship
do not assign personality morality or social rank from posture body angle gaze direction or frame height alone
do not let every figure face the viewer when the scene claims they are acting on one another or on a shared target
do not use identical poses and expressions for all members of an ensemble
do not bury the action target behind effects or costume detail while still claiming a readable relationship
counterexamples: two characters standing shoulder to shoulder with matching smiles show adjacency but no directed relationship event
a taller figure above a shorter figure does not by itself establish authority or dominance
mutual eye contact without an action target consequence or context does not establish intimacy
a protective-looking pose with no visible threat target or response is an unsupported label
a crowded cast collage in which all hands disappear cannot communicate complementary action
boundaries: no protected character costume emblem team composition or signature scene may be reproduced
no relationship label may override visible consent agency or a user's explicit description
no minor-coded participant may be sexualized or placed in an exploitative adult relationship
no disability body type ethnicity gender presentation or age appearance may be used as shorthand for personality status or morality
no proximity-based claim should be presented as a universal psychological or cultural truth
format_implications: single illustrations should expose one complete actor-action-target-consequence chain in the first two reads
key art may add secondary arcs only after the central interaction remains readable at thumbnail scale
card art should keep the target and consequence inside the safe crop rather than relying on off-frame explanation
vertical sequences may distribute trigger action and consequence across reveals while retaining participant identity anchors
viewer_implications: a complementary action gives the viewer evidence to infer a relationship instead of asking them to accept a label
faces can invite social reading while hands and targets answer what is actually happening
a delayed second discovery of the consequence rewards reinspection without obscuring the first read
preserved response agency prevents care conflict and authority scenes from collapsing into stereotypes

title: Unobtrusive tracking of interpersonal orienting and distance predicts the subjective quality of social interactions
abstracted_dimensions: interpersonal distance and joint orientation can be measured relationally rather than as isolated body cues
distance patterns predicted reported interaction quality under minimally constrained conditions
joint orientation related differently to cooperative task effort than distance related to enjoyment
the meaning of a spatial cue depends on task demands and interaction context
limitations: the study concerns live adult dyads rather than drawn ensembles
correlations with reported interaction quality do not license personality inference
the findings do not define universal comfortable distances or culture-independent staging rules
reuse_note: Only contextual proxemics, joint orientation, and task-dependence were abstracted; no participant data, apparatus, image, scene, or prose was copied.

title: Eyes on the Mind: Investigating the Influence of Gaze Dynamics on the Perception of Others in Real-Time Social Interaction
abstracted_dimensions: social gaze can organize triadic interaction among two actors and a physical target
joint and shared attention are distinct interaction structures
reaction timing and congruency affect whether another's response feels contingent on one's action
shared attention required more gaze shifts and more time than simple joint attention in the experiment
limitations: the controlled interaction used virtual figures with largely static faces
dynamic gaze timing must be translated cautiously into a single still image
gaze direction alone does not prove mental state relationship consent or personality
reuse_note: Only shared-target, gaze-contingency, and agency-consequence distinctions were abstracted; no virtual figure, stimulus, interface, person, or prose was copied.

title: Digital character costume design in computer-animated feature films
abstracted_dimensions: costume silhouette material and behavior contribute to recognition embodiment action and narrative
tangible material investigation can inform digitally represented garment behavior
space and objects can preserve indexical traces from earlier events and invite viewer reconstruction
use wear repair alteration and environmental exposure form different trace classes that should not be conflated
continuity requires separating identity invariants from event-dependent state layers across costume prop and environment
limitations: the anchor monograph studies a bounded set of computer-animated feature productions and does not establish one universal costume grammar
the environmental-storytelling source concerns navigable game spaces, so transfer to a single illustration is a design inference
the material-trace source is a technical guide for bronze sculpture and its specific conservation conclusions cannot be generalized to every material
wear damage or repair cannot establish a character's personality class morality or trauma without independent context
reuse_note: Only abstract embodiment, material-response, indexical-trace, and state-ledger mechanisms were retained; no costume, prop, environment, production asset, protected design, or prose was copied.

mechanisms.statement: separate stable identity anchors from event-dependent costume prop and environment state layers
connect garment silhouette material and deformation to the current action instead of treating costume as detached ornament
propagate one event cause across clothing props and surroundings through material-specific responses
distinguish use wear acute damage repair later alteration and environmental deposit by location edge quality and layering
attach every trace to a plausible contact path exposure source or prior action rather than applying uniform distress
maintain an explicit before current and after state ledger across related images
use props and environmental traces as indexical clues that let the viewer reconstruct an earlier event
preserve chronology by showing older wear beneath newer residue repair or replacement

illustration_evidence_definitions.identity_invariant_silhouette_anchor: At least two stable contour, proportion, construction, or attachment features remain recognizable beneath every state overlay.
illustration_evidence_definitions.garment_action_deformation: Folds, tension, compression, drag, or lift align with the character's current pose, force direction, and garment construction.
illustration_evidence_definitions.prop_contact_wear_zone: A worn, polished, stained, repaired, or compressed area occurs where the prop is repeatedly held, placed, struck, opened, or carried.
illustration_evidence_definitions.environment_event_trace: A displaced object, scraped surface, residue boundary, shadow gap, or repair patch records a specific earlier event in the setting.
illustration_evidence_definitions.cross_asset_shared_residue: The same event material appears in physically plausible amounts and contact locations on costume, prop, and nearby environment.
illustration_evidence_definitions.repair_over_damage_layer: A later stitch, patch, brace, replacement piece, or filled break visibly overlaps an older bounded loss or fracture.
illustration_evidence_definitions.material_specific_response: Textile, leather, metal, wood, glass, paper, stone, and painted surfaces react differently to the same force or exposure.
illustration_evidence_definitions.state_ledger_before_after: A compact metadata record states retained invariants, introduced changes, removed changes, and the event that caused each transition.

compatibility: combine a costume change with a prop or environment consequence from the same named event
pair surface wear with the repeated contact that would create it
keep at least two identity anchors unobscured when adding heavy state overlays
use different trace geometry for abrasion impact heat moisture dust and repair
carry persistent changes forward until a stated cleaning repair replacement or recovery event removes them
conflicts: do not apply identical scratches dirt or tears to every material and surface
do not move damage marks or repairs between images without a stated continuity event
do not infer poverty violence occupation personality or morality from wear alone
do not let decorative accessories contradict the shown action weight weather or material behavior
do not use random background clutter as a substitute for an event-specific environmental clue
counterexamples: uniform edge grunge across metal cloth skin and stone communicates a filter rather than shared history
a pristine carried tool beside heavily worn matching holsters breaks the implied use history
a torn sleeve that returns intact in the next state without repair replacement or time transition breaks continuity
a room full of unrelated overturned objects supplies noise but no reconstructable prior event

no person or social group may be assigned character traits from clothing condition or material possessions

model sheets should place invariant identity anchors beside explicit state overlays and transition causes
covers and key art should preserve the most important continuity clue within thumbnail and crop-safe areas
sequential art should carry persistent traces forward and reserve repair or removal for an observable transition
viewer_implications: coherent traces let the viewer reconstruct history instead of merely seeing a distressed surface

layered repair can communicate care maintenance and elapsed time without assigning personality by appearance

title: Game Spaces Speak Volumes: Indexical Storytelling
abstracted_dimensions: spatial design can make past events relevant through evidence embedded in the environment
indexical traces support story construction rather than only backstory exposition
a viewer or player can piece together prior events by reading objects and space
interaction can also leave new traces that extend the environment's history

gameplay relevance does not directly establish commercial image appeal
reuse_note: Only indexical trace, environmental inference, and story-reconstruction mechanisms were abstracted; no level, asset, interface, protected work, or prose was copied.

title: Guidelines for the Technical Examination of Bronze Sculpture
abstracted_dimensions: objects may retain distinguishable traces of fabrication use repair alteration replication exposure and later treatment
surface evidence should be described and mapped before assigning an interpretation
loss coating patina wear deposit and repair can overlap in chronological layers
material traces may be ambiguous and require documentary or analytical corroboration
limitations: the guide concerns real bronze sculpture and is not a universal material-behavior manual
its scientific examination methods are not instructions for fabricating false provenance
fictional design may borrow only the distinction among trace classes and the discipline of marking uncertainty
reuse_note: Only trace-class, chronology, mapping, and uncertainty principles were abstracted; no object, ritual item, treatment procedure, image, or prose was copied.

title: 마법소녀 애니메이션의 변신 시퀀스 구조 변화 연구 - 단일 변신 모델에서 다중 변신 구조로 -
abstracted_dimensions: a transformation sequence can be decomposed into trigger medium visual marker and result
repetition may teach a condition-to-result rule rather than merely repeat one finished form
perceived causality in simple animation depends partly on spatial and temporal event features
stylized effects can be art-directed as a coherent visual system rather than added as generic decoration
a complete causal grammar also needs a bounded cost and aftermath so the result changes what can happen next
limitations: the anchor article analyzes a bounded genre and selected commercial works, so its four-part structure is not a universal law
the causality experiment used simple schematic motions rather than illustrated bodies or supernatural events
the effects source is a production paper about one animated series and does not test viewer comprehension or preference
the required cost and aftermath fields are project design safeguards inferred from causal completeness, not a measured claim that costly transformations are always better
reuse_note: Only abstract trigger, state, condition-result, causal-motion, stylized-effect, cost, and aftermath mechanisms were retained; no transformation bank, character, costume, effect asset, protected design, or prose was copied.

mechanisms.statement: show an explicit trigger or condition at the onset so the transformed result has a visible cause
organize the event as pre-state trigger contact propagation resolved state and aftermath
use a visible medium or transfer path to connect the activating condition with the resulting form
preserve at least two identity invariants while selected state-dependent markers change
make the primary effect follow a directional field and produce material-specific contact responses
encode a bounded cost as spent resource temporary constraint effort recovery need or lost option
show an aftermath residue changed capability or environmental consequence that proves the event mattered
separate the primary causal effect path from secondary decorative accents so ornament cannot replace explanation

illustration_evidence_definitions.transformation_trigger_contact: A hand, device, environmental condition, spoken-action proxy, injury-free gesture, or resource visibly initiates the change.
illustration_evidence_definitions.transformation_phase_boundary: At least two adjacent phases are distinguished by silhouette, value, material, or spatial change rather than a uniform glow.
illustration_evidence_definitions.transformation_medium_path: A continuous beam, ribbon, crack, growth front, fluid path, mechanical linkage, or other generic carrier connects cause to changed region.
illustration_evidence_definitions.transformation_identity_invariant: Two stable facial, proportional, construction, motif, or movement features remain recognizable before and after the state change.
illustration_evidence_definitions.fx_directional_propagation: Effect shapes have a readable origin, travel direction, front, wake, falloff, or orbit consistent with the activation event.
illustration_evidence_definitions.fx_material_interaction: Nearby textile, metal, dust, liquid, foliage, glass, or ground shows a distinct response to the same effect field.
illustration_evidence_definitions.transformation_cost_marker: A visibly depleted meter-independent resource, constrained limb, shortened reach, dropped option, fatigue posture, cooling surface, or recovery action records the price.
illustration_evidence_definitions.transformation_aftermath_residue: Scorched-free discoloration, shed shell, condensed vapor, displaced debris, altered shadow, exhausted medium, or changed environment remains after the peak effect.

compatibility: combine every result state with one visible trigger and one visible aftermath
pair an expanding effect with outward material displacement and a contracting effect with inward pull or residue concentration
preserve identity invariants when costume silhouette hair or body architecture changes
match each selectable state to a distinct condition capability and bounded cost
keep secondary spark particles or flares subordinate to the primary propagation path
conflicts: do not substitute glow sparkles smoke or lens flare for a cause and phase structure
do not grant a new capability without a stated condition limit cost or aftermath
do not let an effect pass through clothing props and environment without any differentiated response

counterexamples: a brighter costume appearing between two frames without trigger medium or residue is a costume swap rather than a causal transformation
a cloud of particles centered on the subject but touching nothing does not establish propagation

sequential art should allocate distinct panels or vertical reveals to trigger propagation resolution and aftermath

card art may depict the resolved state but must retain a trigger remnant cost marker or aftermath inside the crop

phase boundaries create anticipation and reward reconstruction of the event

title: Perceived physical and social causality in animated motions: Spontaneous reports and ratings
abstracted_dimensions: observers can report physical social or noncausal readings from simple animated motion events
causal interpretation depends partly on perceptual event features rather than labels alone
spatial and temporal organization contribute to whether one motion is read as causing another
physical and social causal readings should remain distinct
limitations: the stimuli were simple schematic animations and not character transformations
the study does not prescribe costume design effect style cost or aftermath
perceived causality in motion does not prove narrative truth intent or morality
reuse_note: Only event-feature, contact, timing, and causal-reading distinctions were abstracted; no stimulus sequence, figure, measurement item, or prose was copied.

title: Pixar’s Win or Lose - Stylized FX in an Animated Series
abstracted_dimensions: stylized effects were developed to support distinct episode-level visual languages
effect work required art-directed shape timing rendering and integration rather than default simulation alone
a coherent effect can bridge technical behavior and a chosen graphic look
production constraints and reusable tools influence which stylized variations remain controllable

production-specific tools and assets cannot be treated as universal prompt syntax
no protected effect shape palette asset workflow or series identity may be copied
reuse_note: Only abstract art-direction, controllable variation, graphic coherence, and scene-integration principles were retained; no protected series asset, effect design, tool implementation, image, or prose was copied.

title: Studies of the Behavioral Sequences: The Neuroethological Morphology Concept Crossing Ethology and Functional Morphology
abstracted_dimensions: functional interpretation can be organized as structure performance behavior and ecological outcome rather than appearance alone
behavioral sequences connect morphology with organism-environment interaction

limitations: the sources concern biological research frameworks rather than fantasy illustration quality
real ecomorphological associations can be nonlinear scale-dependent context-dependent or confounded
the matrix supports plausibility and causal coherence but does not require fictional life to obey every terrestrial biological constraint
no creature temperament intelligence morality social value or threat level may be inferred from morphology alone
reuse_note: Only abstract structure, performance, behavior, environment, trade-off, and uncertainty mechanisms were retained; no species anatomy, specimen, sacred being, protected creature, named character, image, or prose was copied.

mechanisms.statement: begin with an ecological task and observable behavior before selecting anatomy

couple locomotion sensing feeding tool use defense or communication to a specific environment contact
show one behavior sequence with initiation target action and result rather than a neutral display pose
constrain joints materials scale and appendage range according to the chosen medium habitat and task
give every specialization at least one visible trade-off limitation or competing demand
treat temperament morality intelligence and social value as unsupported unless behavior and context independently establish them
differentiate silhouettes through functionally meaningful proportions and contacts rather than stacked random anomalies

combine specialization with one trade-off that affects the current action
use environmental traces to corroborate repeated behavior without treating them as proof of temperament
conflicts: do not add wings fins horns eyes tails and armor without assigning separate compatible functions and material support
do not infer aggression gentleness intelligence loyalty or evil from teeth eye count body size color or silhouette
do not give the same appendage incompatible ranges loads or materials in one state
do not place a habitat specialist in a contradictory medium without showing adaptation equipment or distress
do not humanize every creature through upright posture human hands or human facial expressions by default
counterexamples: decorative wings with no load path span clearance or interaction with air do not establish flight function
oversized eyes without a light environment gaze target or sensing behavior remain a cute or uncanny ornament
many limbs repeating the same neutral pose increase complexity without revealing locomotion or task division
heavy armor paired with extreme flexibility and speed but no visible trade-off lacks causal coherence
sharp teeth beside a passive portrait do not establish diet threat behavior or morality
boundaries: no protected creature silhouette anatomy pattern emblem named species or signature behavior may be reproduced
no living religious sacred folkloric or culturally restricted being may be flattened into a generic monster component library
no fictional illustration may be presented as proof of real animal behavior evolution ecology or undiscovered species
no cruelty mutilation forced breeding or graphic predation is required to communicate function
no human group disability body type or cultural dress may be animalized or used as creature shorthand
format_implications: single illustrations should freeze the phase where structure contact behavior target and outcome are simultaneously readable
model sheets should organize views by function range of motion material constraint and state rather than decorative angle alone
key art should retain the functional silhouette and environment contact at thumbnail scale
sequential art may distribute behavior initiation action and result while maintaining body-plan invariants
viewer_implications: functionally connected details invite the viewer to infer how the creature lives rather than merely catalog unusual parts
environment contact supplies weight scale and credibility
a visible trade-off makes specialization feel authored rather than omnipotent
behavior directed toward a target produces character interest without assigning human personality from anatomy
